_comment: C19 TRUST POLICY. Version 1 pinned GitHub's OIDC JWKS leaf keys as an offline root. That was
wrong twice over: those keys ROTATE, so offline verification would break on every rotation,
and a rotating leaf is not a trust anchor. Sigstore keyless does not need them at all — the
OIDC token is exchanged for a short-lived Fulcio certificate at signing time, and a verifier
proves the signer's identity from that certificate's own extensions against a Fulcio root.
The offline anchor is therefore independently bootstrapped Sigstore TUF material, held beside
this file and authenticated by the TUF chain rather than by having been downloaded.

_comment: EXACT values only. A regex identity policy is how a verifier ends up accepting a signature
from a workflow it did not mean to trust — `.*` in the wrong place accepts any branch, any
workflow, or any fork. Every field below has one exact value, so there is nothing to widen.

sigstore-fulcio.description: Fulcio-issued short-lived certificate bound to a GitHub Actions OIDC identity, with the signature recorded in Rekor. The trust root is the TUF-authenticated Sigstore material, not any single rotating key.
